devices: design: the main synth: a wavetable pluck for the attack + a soft saw lead with a late vibrato
design: the supersaw bright (low-pass 6.5 kHz), a 1-semitone rise into each stab, a 1/16 square tremolo
design: percussion full: 16th hats, rolls into each phrase, snaps, tom fills, a shaker, a ride
Kick: tuned to the key (43.7 Hz), 300 ms: in the build on 1, quarters, eighths, a roll; in the drop [0, 1.5, 2.75] / [0, 0.75, 2.5, 3.5] in the bar — the rhythm the bass plays too
Snare + clap: the build's roll (quarters → 32nds, rising, climbing an octave), the breath, one big clap; in the drop a snare a semitone up and a clap together on 3, one room

Percussion: 16th hats accented on the 8ths (8ths with open hats and a ride in the second half), rolls into each phrase, snaps on the e of 2 and 4, a tom fill after every second snare, crashes on the phrase
Shaker: a shaker: a hat tuned up, 35 ms, on the off-sixteenths, right of centre
Reese bass: the verse's reese under the build's first six bars, then gone
Sub: a sine sub, mono, on the chord's root WITH every drop kick (the kick's rhythm is the bassline's), ducked 14 dB by the kick and back within ~200 ms
Mid bass: the bass's voice an octave up: saws and a square, low-passed 1.4 kHz, tube-driven, high-passed at 160 Hz so the sub owns the low end; ducked 14 dB by the kick

Supersaw: two saw stacks (5 voices ±16 ct; 5 an octave up): in the build stabs quickening (halves → sixteenths) as the low-pass opens 350 Hz → 7 kHz; in the drop the melody on top of every chord, each stab rising 1 st into the note over 70 ms, a 1/16 square tremolo (depth 0.45), driven 5 dB, 160 % wide, mono under 180 Hz, pumped 12 dB by the kick
Noise riser: white noise through a low-pass opening 300 Hz → 12 kHz over the build's last four bars, swelling in, cut for the breath
Pitch riser: one supersaw note bent up two octaves over the build's last four bars
Main synth: a pluck (harmonics table) for the attack + a soft saw lead with a late vibrato for the sustain; chorused, an echo, a room — the build's melody (the drop's call teased first)
Airy bell: the verse's bell, answering the build's first half
Impact: the drop's downbeat: an 808 boom punched down two octaves (2.5 s) + the crash; a reversed-cymbal swell (noise, 1.2 s attack) into the drop's second phrase
Reverse cymbal: noise, a 1.2 s attack, high-passed: a cymbal backwards into the drop's ninth bar

elements.recipe: tuned to the key (49.0 Hz), 300 ms: in the build on 1, quarters, eighths, a roll; in the drop [0, 1.75, 2.5] / [0, 0.75, 2.25, 3.5] in the bar — the rhythm the bass plays too

elements.name: Snare + clap
elements.recipe: the build's roll (quarters → 32nds, rising, climbing an octave), the breath, one big clap; in the drop a snare a semitone up and a clap together on 3, one room

elements.name: Percussion
elements.recipe: hats swung (the off-beats 80 ms late) with ghost 16ths, rim on the a's, a cowbell every second bar, a tom fill every four, crashes

elements.name: Shaker
elements.recipe: a shaker: a hat tuned up, 35 ms, on the off-sixteenths, right of centre

elements.name: Reese bass
elements.recipe: the verse's reese under the build's first six bars, then gone

elements.name: Sub
elements.recipe: a sine sub, mono, on the chord's root WITH every drop kick (the kick's rhythm is the bassline's), ducked 14 dB by the kick and back within ~200 ms

elements.name: Mid bass
elements.recipe: the bass's voice an octave up: saws and a square, low-passed 1.4 kHz, tube-driven, high-passed at 160 Hz so the sub owns the low end; ducked 14 dB by the kick

elements.name: Supersaw
elements.recipe: two saw stacks (5 voices ±16 ct; 5 an octave up): in the build stabs quickening (halves → sixteenths) as the low-pass opens 350 Hz → 7 kHz; in the drop the melody on top of every chord, each stab dropping 1.5 st into the note over 90 ms, a 1/16 square tremolo (depth 0.75), driven 5 dB, 160 % wide, mono under 180 Hz, pumped 12 dB by the kick

elements.name: Noise riser
elements.recipe: white noise through a low-pass opening 300 Hz → 12 kHz over the build's last four bars, swelling in, cut for the breath

elements.name: Pitch riser
elements.recipe: one supersaw note bent up two octaves over the build's last four bars

elements.name: Main synth
elements.recipe: a square pluck (pulse table) for the attack + a soft saw lead with a late vibrato for the sustain; chorused, an echo, a room — the build's melody (the drop's call teased first)

elements.name: Airy bell
elements.recipe: the verse's bell, answering the build's first half

elements.name: Impact
elements.recipe: the drop's downbeat: an 808 boom punched down two octaves (2.5 s) + the crash; a reversed-cymbal swell (noise, 1.2 s attack) into the drop's second phrase

elements.name: Reverse cymbal
elements.recipe: noise, a 1.2 s attack, high-passed: a cymbal backwards into the drop's ninth bar

note: same problem, supersaw need more sharp
